metadata.title: Partition relations for $\eta_\alpha$ and for $\aleph_\alpha$-saturated models
metadata.authors: P. Erdos, A. Hajnal, E. C. Milner
metadata.source_note: Extracted from PDF->text fallback; .tex source not available. Math fidelity reduced.
metadata.registry_mismatch_note: metadata.json claims this paper is 'A Note on Hamiltonian Circuits' by Chvatal, Erdos (1972), but the PDF source actually contains Erdos-Hajnal-Milner 1972, 'Partition relations for $\eta_\alpha$ and for $\aleph_\alpha$-saturated models' (Theory of Sets and Topology, Berlin 1972, pp. 95-108). Extraction reflects the actual PDF content.

nodes.name: $R_\alpha$ and $\eta_\alpha$
nodes.statement: $R_\alpha$ is the set of all $0,1$-sequences of length $\omega_\alpha$ that have a final $1$. Its order type under lexicographic order is denoted $\eta_\alpha$.
nodes.statement_clean: Defines the universal embedding set $R_\alpha$ and its lexicographic order type $\eta_\alpha$, the higher-cardinal analogue of the rationals.

nodes.name: Graph and independent / complete bipartite subgraph
nodes.statement: A graph is $G=(S,E)$ with $E \subset [S]^2$. A set $X \subset S$ is independent if $[X]^2 \cap E = \emptyset$; $[M,N] = \{\{x,y\}: x \in M, y \in N, x \neq y\}$ is a complete bipartite subgraph if $[M,N] \subset E$ and $M \cap N = \emptyset$.

nodes.name: $\aleph_\alpha$-quasi filter
nodes.statement:
$\mathcal{F}$ is an $\aleph_\alpha$-quasi filter on $E$ if $\emptyset 
otin \mathcal{F}$, $\mathcal{F} 
eq \emptyset$, and whenever $F_0 \supset F_1 \supset \cdots \supset F_
u \supset \cdots$ ($
u < \lambda < \omega_\alpha$) is a non-increasing sequence in $\mathcal{F}$, there is $F \in \mathcal{F}$ with $F \subset  igcap_
u F_
u$.

nodes.name: Dense set in a quasi filter
nodes.statement: Let $\mathcal{F}$ be an $\aleph_\alpha$-quasi filter on $E$ and $F \in \mathcal{F}$. A set $A \subset E$ is dense in $F$ if $A \cap F' \neq \emptyset$ for every $F' \in \mathcal{F}$ with $F' \subset F$. Set $\mathrm{Dense}(\mathcal{F}) = \{A \subset E : A \text{ dense in some } F \in \mathcal{F}\}$ and $\mathrm{ND}(\mathcal{F}) = \mathcal{P}(E) \setminus \mathrm{Dense}(\mathcal{F})$.

nodes.statement_clean: Generalizes the Erdos-Rado partition symbol to allow entries that are families of subsets of $[E]^r$ rather than just cardinals.

nodes.name: Bipartite-entry shorthand $[m, \Theta]$
nodes.statement: If $r=2$, $\Theta \subset \mathcal{P}(E)$, the entry $\mathcal{O}_\nu = \{[M,N] : M \subset E, N \in \Theta, M \cap N = \emptyset, |M| = m\}$ is abbreviated $[m, \Theta]$ in the partition symbol.

nodes.name: $\eta_\alpha$-set (Hausdorff property $P_\alpha$)
nodes.statement: $(S,<)$ is an $\eta_\alpha$-set if it has property $P_\alpha$: whenever $A,B \subset S$, $A < B$ and $|A|, |B| < \aleph_\alpha$, there is $x \in S$ with $A < \{x\} < B$.

nodes.name: Finite intersection property
nodes.statement: A family $\mathcal{G}$ of sets has the finite intersection property (f.i.p.) if $\bigcap \mathcal{G}' \neq \emptyset$ for every finite subfamily $\mathcal{G}' \subset \mathcal{G}$.

nodes.name: $\aleph_\alpha$-saturated family
nodes.statement: A family $\mathcal{G}$ is $\aleph_\alpha$-saturated if $\bigcap \mathcal{G}' \neq \emptyset$ whenever $\mathcal{G}' \subset \mathcal{G}$, $|\mathcal{G}'| < \aleph_\alpha$, and $\mathcal{G}'$ has the finite intersection property.

nodes.name: $\aleph_\alpha$-saturated relational system
nodes.statement: Let $\mathfrak{A} = \langle A, R_\lambda\rangle_{\lambda<\mu}$ be a relational system of type $\Sigma_\alpha$. With $\Phi(\mathfrak{A}) = \{E^{\mathfrak{A}}(\Phi, a_1,\ldots,a_n) : \Phi \in F(\mu)\}$ the set of definable subsets of $A$, $\mathfrak{A}$ is $\aleph_\alpha$-saturated if $\Phi(\mathfrak{A})$ is $\aleph_\alpha$-saturated.

nodes.name: $\mathrm{ND}(\mathcal{F})$ is an $\aleph_\alpha$-complete proper ideal
nodes.statement: If $\mathcal{F}$ is an $\aleph_\alpha$-quasi filter on $E$, then $\mathrm{ND}(\mathcal{F})$ is an $\aleph_\alpha$-complete proper ideal in $\mathcal{P}(E)$.

nodes.name: Open intervals of $R_\alpha$
nodes.statement: Let $E = R_\alpha$ and $\mathcal{F}$ be the set of all non-empty open intervals $(a,b)$ in $R_\alpha$ with $a, b \in R_\alpha \cup \{-\infty, \infty\}$. Then $\mathcal{F}$ is an $\aleph_{\mathrm{cf}(\alpha)}$-quasi filter; $A \in \mathrm{Dense}(\mathcal{F})$ iff $A$ is dense in some interval $(a,b)$.

nodes.name: Sufficient condition for $|A| \geq \aleph_\alpha$
nodes.statement: Let $\mathcal{F}$ be an $\aleph_\alpha$-quasi filter on $E$. Then $A \in \mathrm{Dense}(\mathcal{F})$ implies $|A| \geq \aleph_\alpha$ provided that whenever $B \subset E$, $|B| < \aleph_\alpha$, $F \in \mathcal{F}$, there is $P \subset F \setminus B$ with $P \in \mathcal{F}$.
assumptions: for $B \subset E$ with $|B|<\aleph_\alpha$ and $F \in \mathcal{F}$, some $P \subset F\setminus B$ lies in $\mathcal{F}$

nodes.name: Partition relation (6) (Erdos-Milner-Rado)
nodes.statement: If $\alpha = \mathrm{cf}(\alpha) > \beta$ and $\aleph_\gamma^m < \aleph_\alpha$ holds for all $\gamma < \alpha$ and $m < \aleph_\beta$, and if $2^{\aleph_\alpha} = \aleph_{\alpha+1}$, then $\eta_\alpha \to (\eta_\alpha, \aleph_\beta)^2$.
nodes.origin_citation: Erdos, Milner, Rado, J. London Math. Soc. 3 (1971) 193-204

nodes.name: Corollary (7) of (6)
nodes.statement: (GCH) $\eta_{\alpha+1} \to (\eta_{\alpha+1}, \aleph_{\alpha+1})^2$.

nodes.name: Generalized partition relation (8)
nodes.statement: Let $\mathcal{F}$ be an $\aleph_{\mathrm{cf}(\alpha)}$-quasi filter on $E$ with $|\mathcal{F}| \leq \aleph_\alpha$. If $\alpha = \mathrm{cf}(\alpha) > \beta$ and $\aleph_\gamma^m < \aleph_\alpha$ for $\gamma < \alpha$, $m < \aleph_\beta$, then $E \to (\mathrm{Dense}(\mathcal{F}), \aleph_\beta)^2$.

nodes.name: Partition relation (9) — corollary of (8)
nodes.statement: (GCH) Let $\mathcal{F}$ be an $\aleph_{\alpha+1}$-quasi filter on $E$ with $|\mathcal{F}| \leq \aleph_{\alpha+1}$. Then $E \to (\mathrm{Dense}(\mathcal{F}), \aleph_{\alpha+1})^2$.

nodes.name: Theorem (10) — first main result
nodes.statement: (GCH) Let $\mathcal{F}$ be an $\aleph_\alpha$-quasi filter on $E$ and suppose $|\mathcal{F}| \leq \aleph_\alpha$, $m^+ < \aleph_{\mathrm{cf}(\alpha)}$. Then $E \to (\mathrm{Dense}(\mathcal{F}), [m, \mathrm{Dense}(\mathcal{F})])^2$.

nodes.name: Corollary (11) of Theorem (10)
nodes.statement: (GCH) If $m^+ < \aleph_\alpha = \aleph_{\mathrm{cf}(\alpha)}$, then $\eta_\alpha \to (\eta_\alpha, [m, \eta_\alpha])^2$.

nodes.name: Negative result (12)
nodes.statement: (GCH) $\aleph_{\alpha+1} \not\to (\aleph_{\alpha+1}, [\aleph_\alpha, \aleph_{\alpha+1}])^2$.
nodes.origin_citation: Erdos-Hajnal-Rado, Acta Math. Acad. Sci. Hung. 16 (1965) Theorem 17

nodes.name: Theorem (13) — second main result
nodes.statement: (GCH) Let $\mathcal{F}$ be an $\aleph_{\beta+1}$-quasi filter on $E$ with $|\mathcal{F}| \leq \aleph_{\beta+1}$. Then $E \to (\mathrm{Dense}(\mathcal{F}), [\aleph_\beta, \aleph_\beta])^2$.

nodes.name: Corollary (14) of Theorem (13)
nodes.statement: (GCH) $\eta_{\beta+1} \to (\eta_{\beta+1}, [\aleph_\beta, \aleph_\beta])^2$.

nodes.name: Strengthening (14) to $[\eta_\beta, \eta_\beta]$
nodes.statement: It is unknown whether (14) can be strengthened by replacing $[\aleph_\beta, \aleph_\beta]$ by $[\eta_\beta, \eta_\beta]$. Simplest case: does $\eta_1 \to (\eta_1, [\eta_0, \eta_0])^2$ hold?

nodes.name: $\eta_1 \to (\eta_1, \eta_0)^2$ from trivial relation
nodes.statement: $\eta_1 \to (\eta_1, \eta_0)^2$ follows from the trivial relation $\eta_1 \to (\omega, \omega^*)$ (Erdos-Rado [4], Theorem 19).

nodes.name: Negative example (15) for singular $\aleph_\alpha$
nodes.statement: $\aleph_\omega \not\to (\aleph_1, [1, \aleph_\omega])^2$ — shown by considering the graph $(S, E)$ with $S = \bigcup_n S_n$, $|S_n|=\aleph_n$, $E = \bigcup [S_n]^2$. Hence (11) is invalid for singular $\aleph_\alpha$.

nodes.name: Theorem (16) — third main result for limit cardinals
nodes.statement: (GCH) If $m < \aleph_\lambda < \aleph_\alpha$, $\alpha = \lambda + 1$, then $\eta_\alpha \to (\eta_\alpha, [m, \eta_\lambda])^2$.

nodes.name: (16) for $m \geq \aleph_\lambda$
nodes.statement: Unknown whether (16) holds when $m \geq \aleph_\lambda$. Simplest cases: does $\eta_\omega \to (\eta_\omega, [\aleph_0, \eta_0])^2$ hold? Does $\eta_\omega \to (\eta_\omega, [\aleph_0, \aleph_0])^2$ hold?

nodes.name: Easy partition for circuits of length $k$
nodes.statement: It is easy to prove that $\eta_\omega \to (\aleph_\omega, [\aleph_k, \aleph_k])^2$ for $k < \omega$.

nodes.name: Even circuits implication of (16)
nodes.statement: If $C_k$ denotes the class of all circuits of length $k$, then (16) implies $(GCH)\ \eta_\omega \to (\eta_\omega, C_{2k})^2$ for every $k<\omega$.

nodes.name: Odd circuits in graphs on $R_\omega$
nodes.statement: Unknown whether $\eta_\omega \to (\eta_\omega, C_{2k+1})^2$ holds for any fixed $k<\omega$. (A graph on $R_\omega$ with no independent set of type $\eta_\omega$ is not 2-chromatic and thus contains odd circuits — but does it contain an odd circuit of fixed size?)

nodes.name: 1-way infinite path partition
nodes.statement: (GCH) $\eta_\alpha \to (\eta_\alpha, P^\infty)^2$ if $\mathrm{cf}(\alpha) > 0$, where $P^\infty$ is the class of 1-way infinite paths in a graph. Follows easily from (7) and (16).

nodes.name: Universality of $\eta_\alpha$-sets
nodes.statement: (i) If $(S,<)$ is an $\eta_\alpha$-set, then $S$ is $\aleph_\alpha$-universal, i.e. $\mathrm{tp}\,S \geq \theta$ whenever $|\theta| \leq \aleph_\alpha$. (ii) If $\aleph_\alpha$ is regular then $R_\alpha$ is an $\eta_\alpha$-set; if (5) holds, every $\eta_\alpha$-set contains a subset similar to $R_\alpha$.

nodes.name: Equivalence of $P_\alpha$ and saturation (18)
nodes.statement: $(S,<)$ has property $P_\alpha$ iff $S$ is densely ordered and the family of intervals $I(S)$ is $\aleph_\alpha$-saturated.

nodes.name: $I(S)$ is a quasi filter (19)
nodes.statement: If $(S,<)$ has property $P_\alpha$, then $I(S)$ is an $\aleph_\alpha$-quasi filter on $S$.

nodes.name: Converse of (19) fails
nodes.statement: The converse of (19) fails even for densely ordered $S$. For example, if $\mathrm{tp}\,S = \eta_2 \omega + \eta_2 \omega^*$, then $S$ is densely ordered and $I(S)$ is an $\aleph_2$-quasi filter, but $I(S)$ is not $\aleph_2$-saturated.

nodes.name: Dense subsets of $\eta_\alpha$-sets contain $\eta_\alpha$-sets (20)
nodes.statement: If $(S,<)$ is an $\eta_\alpha$-set and $A \in \mathrm{Dense}(I(S))$, then $A$ contains an $\eta_\alpha$-set.

nodes.name: Dense subsets of $R_\alpha$ have type $\geq \eta_\alpha$ (21)
nodes.statement: If $A \in \mathrm{Dense}(I(R_\alpha))$, then $\mathrm{tp}\,A \geq \eta_\alpha$.

nodes.name: Proof of (20)
nodes.statement: Suppose $A$ dense in $X=(a,b)$. Take $A',B' \subset A \cap X$ with $A' < B'$, $|A'|,|B'|<\aleph_\alpha$. By $P_\alpha$ pick $a',b' \in S$ with $A' \cup \{a\} < \{a'\} < \{b'\} < B' \cup \{b\}$; density gives $x \in A \cap (a',b')$ between $A'$ and $B'$, so $A \cap X$ is an $\eta_\alpha$-set.

nodes.name: Proof of (21)
nodes.statement: Uses Harzheim's result that $\eta_\alpha^{\aleph_\alpha} = \eta_\alpha$ and Harzheim's max-construction. Suppose $A$ dense in interval $X$ of $R_\alpha$ with $\mathrm{tp}\,X = \eta_\alpha$; $X$ contains disjoint intervals $I_x$ ($x \in R_\alpha$) with $I_x < I_y$ when $x<y$, and $A \cap I_x \neq \emptyset$.

nodes.name: Hypothesis (22) for proofs of (10), (13), (16)
nodes.statement: (a) GCH; (b) $\mathcal{F}$ is an $\aleph_{\mathrm{cf}(\alpha)}$-quasi filter on $E$ with $|\mathcal{F}| \leq \aleph_\alpha$; (c) $[E]^2 = \mathcal{Z}_0 \cup \mathcal{Z}_1$ is a 2-partition such that $[A]^2 \not\subset \mathcal{Z}_0$ whenever $A \in \mathrm{Dense}(\mathcal{F})$.

nodes.name: Edge-neighbour notation $Z_i(x), Z_i(X)$
nodes.statement: For $x \in E$ and $i<2$, $Z_i(x) = \{y \in E : \{x,y\} \in \mathcal{Z}_i\}$. For $X \subset E$, $Z_i(X) = \bigcap_{x \in X} Z_i(x)$.

nodes.name: Lemma (23) — first stepping-down lemma
nodes.statement: Suppose (22)(b),(c) hold and $C \subset F \in \mathcal{F}$. Then there exist $A \subset C$, $F' \subset F$ with $A \cap F' = \emptyset$, $|A| < \aleph_\alpha$, $F' \in \mathcal{F}$, and $C \cap F' \subset \bigcup_{x \in A} Z_0(x)$.
conclusions: $\exists A\subset C, F'\subset F$ with $A \cap F' = \emptyset$, $|A|<\aleph_\alpha$, $F' \in \mathcal{F}$, $C \cap F' \subset \bigcup_{x\in A} Z_0(x)$

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma (23)
nodes.statement:
Enumerate $\{F'' \in \mathcal{F} : F'' \subset F\}$ as $F_
u$ ($
u < \omega_\alpha$), $F_0=F$. Suppose lemma fails; build $a_
u \in C$ by transfinite induction so $A=\{a_
u\}$ is dense in $\mathcal{F}$ with $[A]^2 \subset \mathcal{Z}_0$, contradicting (22)(c).

nodes.name: Lemma (24) — strengthened stepping-down
nodes.statement: Suppose (22)(b),(c) hold and $m < \aleph_{\mathrm{cf}(\alpha)}$, $C \subset F \in \mathcal{F}$. Then there exist $A \subset C$, $F' \subset F$ with $A \cap F' = \emptyset$, $|A| < \aleph_\alpha$, $F' \in \mathcal{F}$, and $|A \cap Z_1(x)| \geq m$ for all $x \in F' \cap C$.
conclusions: $\exists A\subset C, F'\subset F$ with $A \cap F'=\emptyset$, $|A|<\aleph_\alpha$, $F'\in\mathcal{F}$, $|A\cap Z_1(x)|\ge m$ for $x\in F'\cap C$

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma (24)
nodes.statement:
Iterate Lemma (23) by transfinite induction along the initial ordinal of cardinality $m$, picking nested $F_
u$ and disjoint $A_
u$. Take $A =  igcup A_
u$; intersection condition gives $|A \cap Z_1(x)| \geq m$ for $x \in F' \cap C$.

nodes.name: Lemma (25) — small subset cover
nodes.statement: (GCH) Let $|X| = \aleph_\beta < \aleph_\alpha$, $m^+ < \aleph_\alpha$. Suppose if $\beta+1 = \alpha$, $m = \aleph_\beta$, then $\mathrm{cf}(\gamma) \neq \mathrm{cf}(\beta)$. Then there is $U_m(X) \subset [X]^m$ with $|U_m(X)| < \aleph_\alpha$ such that every $Y \in [X]^m$ has $Y \supset Z$ for some $Z \in U_m(X)$.

nodes.name: Necessity of cofinality condition in (25)
nodes.statement: If $\beta+1=\alpha$, $m=\aleph_\beta$, and $\mathrm{cf}(\gamma)=\mathrm{cf}(\beta)$, then no set $U_m(X)$ with the stated property exists unless $|U_m(X)| \geq \aleph_\alpha$.

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma (25)
nodes.statement:
Case $ eta+1<\alpha$: take $U_m(X)=[X]^m$ since $|[X]^m| \leq \aleph_ eta^m < \aleph_\alpha$ under GCH. Case $ eta+1=\alpha$: write $X =  igcup_{
u<\omega_ eta} X_
u$ with $|X_
u|<\aleph_ eta$ and put $U_m(X) =  igcup_
u  igcup_{\mu<
u}[X_\mu]^m$; cofinality hypothesis ensures every $m$-subset is non-cofinal.

nodes.name: Lemma (27) — combined cover lemma
nodes.statement: Suppose (22)(a)(b)(c) hold, $C \subset F \in \mathcal{F}$, $m^+ < \aleph_\alpha$, and (26) holds. Then there exist $A \subset C$, $F' \subset F$ with $|A| < \aleph_\alpha$, $F' \in \mathcal{F}$, $A \cap F' = \emptyset$ and $C \cap F' \subset \bigcup\{Z_1(B) : B \in U_m(A)\}$.

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma (27)
nodes.statement: Combine (24) (gives $A,F'$ with $|A \cap Z_1(x)|\geq m$) and (25) (gives $U_m(A)$): each $x \in F'$ has some $B \in U_m(A)$ with $A \cap Z_1(x) \supset B$, i.e. $x \in Z_1(B)$.

nodes.name: Proof of Theorem (10)
nodes.statement: From hypothesis $m^+ \leq \aleph_{\mathrm{cf}(\alpha)}$, (22)(a),(b) hold; assume (22)(c). Verify (26) holds (vacuously for limit $\alpha$; from $m<\aleph_\beta$ for regular $\aleph_\beta$; by replacing $m$ by larger regular cardinal otherwise). Apply Lemma (27) with $C=F$ to get $A, F'$; (1) and (27) give $Z_1(B) \in \mathrm{Dense}(\mathcal{F})$ for some $B \in U_m(A)$, so $[B, Z_1(B)] \subset \mathcal{Z}_1$.

nodes.name: Verify hypothesis (26)
nodes.statement: If $\alpha$ limit, (26) holds vacuously. If $\alpha=\beta+1$ and $\aleph_\beta$ regular, $m^+ \leq \aleph_{\mathrm{cf}(\alpha)}$ gives $m<\aleph_\beta^{\aleph_{\mathrm{cf}(\beta)}}$. If $\aleph_\beta$ singular, replace $m$ by larger regular cardinal with $\aleph_{\mathrm{cf}(\beta)} < m < \aleph_\beta$.

nodes.name: Apply Lemma (27)
nodes.statement: Set $C = F \in \mathcal{F}$ and apply Lemma (27) to get $A, F'$. Then $C \cap F' = F' \in \mathrm{Dense}(\mathcal{F})$.

nodes.name: Find good $B$ via the small-cover ideal
nodes.statement: By (25) $|U_m(A)| < \aleph_\alpha$; by (1) [$\mathrm{ND}(\mathcal{F})$ ideal] and (27), some $B \in U_m(A)$ has $Z_1(B) \in \mathrm{Dense}(\mathcal{F})$. Then $[B, Z_1(B)] \subset \mathcal{Z}_1$ and $|B|=m$ as required.

nodes.name: Proof of Theorem (16)
nodes.statement: Set $E=R_\alpha$, $\mathcal{F}=I(R_\alpha)$. Apply Lemma (27) with $C=F=R_\alpha$ to get $A, F'=(a,b)$. Since $\mathrm{tp}\,F'=\eta_\alpha$ and $\lambda<\alpha$, by (21) some $R \subset F'$ has $\mathrm{tp}\,R = \eta_\lambda$. By (25) and (21), some $B \in U_m(A)$ has $\mathrm{tp}(Z_1(B) \cap R) \geq \eta_\lambda$, giving $[B, Z_1(B)] \subset \mathcal{Z}_1$.

nodes.statement:
Use ramification argument from [2, Lemma 1]. With $\alpha= eta+1$, can assume $ eta>\mathrm{cf}( eta)$. Build a tree of length $\sigma=\omega_{\mathrm{cf}( eta)}$ with sets $F_\sigma, S'(
u), A(
u)$ for $
u \in N_\sigma$ and $F_{\sigma+1}, S(
u), B(
u)$ for $
u \in N_{\sigma+1}$. After construction, find $
u \in N_\sigma$ with $ igcap_\sigma S(
u estriction \sigma+1) 
eq \emptyset$; setting $B_\sigma = B(
u estriction \sigma+1)$, $C =  igcup_{\sigma 	ext{ even}} B_\sigma$, $D =  igcup_{\sigma 	ext{ odd}} B_\sigma$ gives $|C|=|D|=\aleph_ eta$, disjoint, with $[C,D] \subset \mathcal{Z}_1$.

nodes.statement:
Choose regular cardinals $\aleph_{\mathrm{cf}( eta)}<m_0<m_1<\cdots<m_\sigma<\cdots<\aleph_ eta=\sup_\sigma m_\sigma$ for $\sigma<ho:=\omega_{\mathrm{cf}( eta)}$. Define index trees $N_\sigma = \{

u_	au)_{	au<\sigma} :

nodes.statement:
By (22)(b) there is $P \in \mathcal{F}$ with $P \subset  igcap_{\sigma<ho} F_{\sigma+1}$. By (32), $\exists

nodes.name: Build $C, D$ from even/odd blocks
nodes.statement: $|B_\sigma| = m_\sigma$ and for $\sigma<\sigma'$ the sets $B_\sigma, B_{\sigma'}$ are disjoint with $[B_\sigma, B_{\sigma'}] \subset \mathcal{Z}_1$. Set $C = \bigcup_{\sigma \text{ even}} B_\sigma$, $D = \bigcup_{\sigma \text{ odd}} B_\sigma$; then $|C|=|D|=\aleph_\beta$, $C \cap D = \emptyset$, $[C,D] \subset \mathcal{Z}_1$.

nodes.name: Property (36): consistent quasi filter / family pair
nodes.statement: Sets $A$ and $\mathcal{O} \subset \mathcal{P}(A)$ satisfy (36) if there is an $\aleph_{\beta+1}$-quasi filter $\mathcal{F}$ on $A$ with $|\mathcal{F}| \leq \aleph_{\beta+1}$ such that for every $X \in \mathrm{Dense}(\mathcal{F})$ there is $Y \in \mathcal{O}$ with $Y \subset X$.

nodes.name: Example (37) — saturated relational system
nodes.statement: (GCH) Let $\mathfrak{A} = \langle A, R_\lambda\rangle_{\lambda<\mu}$ be an $\aleph_{\beta+1}$-saturated relational system, $|\mathfrak{A}|=|A|=\aleph_{\beta+1}$, $\mu < \omega_{\beta+1}$. Let $\mathcal{O}$ be the set of $X \subset A$ for which there is $A'$, $X \subset A' \subset A$, satisfying: (i) $\mathfrak{A}' = \mathfrak{A} \restriction A'$ is $\aleph_{\beta+1}$-saturated and $|\mathfrak{A}'|=\aleph_{\beta+1}$; (ii) $X \cap B \neq \emptyset$ for every infinite $B \in \Phi(\mathfrak{A}')$; (iii) $\Phi(\mathfrak{A}') \restriction X$ is $\aleph_{\beta+1}$-saturated. Then $A, \mathcal{O}$ satisfy (36).

nodes.name: Example (38) — sharper saturated example
nodes.statement: Same hypothesis as (37). Suppose further that for every $\Phi \in F(\mu)$ with $n+1$ free variables and $a_1,\ldots,a_n \in A$, $|E^{\mathfrak{A}}(\Phi, a_1,\ldots,a_n) \setminus \{a_1,\ldots,a_n\}| = |E^{\mathfrak{A}}(\Phi, a_1,\ldots,a_n)|$ when $\geq \aleph_0$. Then $A$ and $\mathcal{O}' = \{X \subset A : \mathfrak{A} \restriction X \text{ is } \aleph_{\beta+1}\text{-saturated of power } \aleph_{\beta+1}\}$ satisfy (36).

nodes.name: Counter-remark of Keisler
nodes.statement: (H. J. Keisler) There exist $\aleph_{\beta+1}$-saturated relational systems for which $\mathcal{O}$ in (37) satisfies (36) but $\mathcal{O}'$ in (38) does not. The extra condition of (38) holds when $\mathfrak{A} = (A,<)$ with $<$ a dense order.

nodes.name: Outline proof of (37)
nodes.statement: Use Keisler's Theorem 2.1 to write $\mathfrak{A} = \mathfrak{B}^I/D$ for an $\aleph_{\beta+1}$-good ultrafilter $D$. Set $\mathcal{F}_0 = \{F \subset A : F = \prod F_i/D, F_i \in \Phi(\mathfrak{B})\}$; show conditions $(\alpha), (\beta)$ hold. Put $\mathcal{F} = \mathcal{F}_0 \cap [A]^{\aleph_{\beta+1}}$. Verify (i), (ii), (iii) of (37) for $X = X' \cap A'$.

nodes.name: Outline proof of (38)
nodes.statement: Use $\mathfrak{B}, \mathfrak{A}, \mathcal{F}_0, X, A'$ from proof of (37). Additional assumption gives $|E^{\mathfrak{A}}(\Phi,\bar a) \setminus \{a_1,\ldots,a_n\}| = |E^{\mathfrak{A}}(\Phi,\bar a)|$ in $A'$. By (37)(ii), $\mathfrak{A}'$ is an elementary extension of $\mathfrak{A} \restriction X$, so $\mathfrak{A} \restriction X = \mathfrak{A}' \restriction X$ is $\aleph_{\beta+1}$-saturated.

nodes.name: Example (39) — $\aleph_{\beta+1}$-complete ideal
nodes.statement: (GCH) Let $\mathcal{S}$ be an $\aleph_{\beta+1}$-complete ideal in $A$ generated by at most $\aleph_{\beta+1}$ elements and let $\mathcal{O} = \mathcal{P}(A) \setminus \mathcal{S}$. Then (36) holds.

nodes.name: Example (40) — measure and category on $\mathbb{R}$
nodes.statement: (GCH) Let $R$ be the set of reals; let $\mathcal{O}_1$ = subsets of positive Lebesgue outer measure; let $\mathcal{O}_2$ = subsets of second category. Then (36) holds with $\beta=0$, $A=R$, $\mathcal{O} = \mathcal{O}_i$ for $i=1,2$.

nodes.name: Partition relations from (36)
nodes.statement: If GCH holds and $A, \mathcal{O}$ satisfy (36), then $A \to (\mathcal{O}, \aleph_{\beta+1})^2$, $A \to (\mathcal{O}, [m, \mathcal{O}])^2$ for $m<\aleph_\beta$, and $A \to (\mathcal{O}, [\aleph_\beta, \aleph_\beta])^2$.
